name: Crunchy Bridge
tagline: Crunchy Data's developer-friendly managed Postgres across AWS, GCP and Azure, now owned by Snowflake.
description: Crunchy Bridge is the managed PostgreSQL service from Crunchy Data, a long-time Postgres contributor whose team joined Snowflake in 2025 and now builds Snowflake Postgres. Bridge runs community Postgres on AWS, Google Cloud or Azure, with superuser-level access, a broad extension set (PostGIS, pgvector, pg_cron, pg_partman), per-minute billing and strong support from Postgres experts. Its analytics offering embeds a DuckDB-based engine to query and write Iceberg and Parquet data in object storage from Postgres. Bridge remains on sale and supported, but new feature investment is now directed at Snowflake Postgres, so weigh the roadmap if you are starting fresh.
statusNote: Crunchy Data was acquired by Snowflake in June 2025; Bridge is still sold and supported while the team builds Snowflake Postgres.

license.name: Proprietary (managed service; engine is PostgreSQL License)

pricing.notes: Billed per minute for compute and storage, invoiced monthly; low-cost hobby instances; backups included.

scale.notes: Vertical scaling with HA standby and read replicas, including cross-region and cross-cloud replicas.

strengths: Runs on AWS, GCP or Azure with cross-cloud replicas
Superuser-level access and a wide extension catalog
Postgres expert support from long-time core contributors
Iceberg/Parquet analytics from Postgres via an embedded DuckDB engine
weaknesses: Roadmap uncertainty after the Snowflake acquisition
No free tier, branching or scale-to-zero
Smaller platform surface than hyperscaler Postgres services
useCases: Production Postgres for teams wanting cloud choice
Querying data lakes in Iceberg from Postgres
Teams that value hands-on Postgres expertise in support
notIdealFor: Hobby projects needing a free tier
